content: ## Metadata_Start ## code: en ## title: Authentication via iframe ## slug: authentication-via-iframe ## seoTitle: ## description: ## contentType: Markdown ## Metadata_End ## Overview Blackthorn offers two types of {{variable.Product_Events}} embedding and authentication: a community component and iframing. Embedding via the Blackthorn Events Listing component allows users to add the Lightning Web component to their Community page. The Events Listing component does not use SSO authentication. Instead, the component authorizes the Community user by comparing the logged-in user with the {{variable.Object_Contact}} record. With iframing, you can add an {{variable.Object_Event}} or {{variable.Object_EventGroup}} directly to your website or community. It also allows for additional customization that is unavailable on the Events Listing component and is often used as an alternative in communities. Authentication relates an external user to a {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} {{variable.Object_Contact}} and uses a key/value pairing from the Context Key (“Key”) and the SSO/Authorization Token (“Token”). Now, {{variable.Product_Events}} can support dynamic visibility of {{variable.Object_Event}}s, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}s (Tickets), {{variable.Object_Session}}s, and more. The process uses only the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}, instead of the entire {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} authentication process, to pass the authenticated “user” to the Blackthorn {{variable.Product_Events}} app’s [iframe](/v1/docs/blackthorn-events-iframes){target=`_blank`}. The two primary uses are as follows: * to allow visibility control of {{variable.Object_Event}}s and related records to different types of {{variable.Object_Contact}}s * to automatically pre-populate {{variable.Object_Contact}} details for registration ## Set Up Authentication :::(Warning) (Mobile Check-in App) SSO is not supported on the Events Mobile Check-in app. ::: ### What is an SSO Code? An SSO code is an authentication method that enables users to authenticate the Events app securely. ### How Iframe Authentication Works 1. An {{variable.Object_Attendee}} logs into a website or a Community that uses iframes. 2. The {{variable.Product_Events}} app pulls the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}. 3. When the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} goes to the iframe, your SSO generation code will run and generates a token. 4. The SSO generation code then uses the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}} from Step 2. ### Setup Process #### Pre-requisite The SSO key generator must be dynamic (or be able to take in any {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}} and spit out an SSO key) to work on multiple Contacts. If you hardcode a {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}, authentication will only work for that Contact. #### Start Here To use Blackthorn {{variable.Product_Events}} authentication for {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}, complete the steps below. 1. Embed the {{variable.Product_Events}} app via [iframe](https://docs.blackthorn.io/v1/docs/blackthorn-events-iframes){target=`_blank`}. 2. Generate a Context Key (e.g., Shared Secret) with valid UTG-8 characters using a key generation tool (ex. [https://guidgenerator.com/online-guid-generator.aspx](https://guidgenerator.com/online-guid-generator.aspx){target=`_blank`}). 3. Encode the Context Key to base64 with an [encoding tool](https://www.base64encode.org/){target=`_blank`}. 4. Send the Context Key and Org ID securely to admin@blackthorn.io if your {{variable.Product_Events}} app is live. * Blackthorn will respond to your request within 1-3 business days. * Do not send the Context Key within cases or to other Blackthorn emails. * Send one Context Key per Salesforce org. 5. Dynamically generate a Token by writing SSO code. The SSO code is the trigger that authenticates a {{variable.Object_Contact}} within the {{variable.Product_Events}} app. 6. Your organization is responsible for writing the SSO code and implementing the process. Here is a code sample you can base your code on: [ssogenerator.pseudo](https://gist.github.com/cryptolos/76c07359b73c3b7f9eea25a6e22db620){target=`_blank`}. The script must be applied to the programming language you are using,, where the codes need to be generated. The Subject ID listed in the pseudocode is the {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}. 7. Add the SSO code (`data-sso`) to the iframe. ```HTML ``` #### Using a 3rd-party Open Authentication Protocol Complete the steps below to use Blackthorn {{variable.Product_Events}} authentication with your 3rd-party open authentication protocol (such as OpenID, Okta, etc.). 1. Embed the {{variable.Product_Events}} app via [iframe](https://docs.blackthorn.io/v1/docs/blackthorn-events-iframes){target=`_blank`}. 2. Generate a Context Key (e.g., Shared Secret) with valid UTG-8 characters using a key generation tool (ex. [https://guidgenerator.com/online-guid-generator.aspx](https://guidgenerator.com/online-guid-generator.aspx){target=`_blank`}). 3. Encode the Context Key to base64 with an [encoding tool](https://www.base64encode.org/){target=`_blank`}. 4. Send the Context Key securely to Blackthorn Onboarding or Support if your {{variable.Product_Events}} app is live. * Blackthorn will respond to your request within 1-3 business days. * Do not send the Context Key within cases or to other Blackthorn emails. * Send one Context Key per Salesforce org. 5. Dynamically generate a Token by writing SSO code. The SSO code is the trigger that authenticates a Contact within the Events app. 6. Your organization is responsible for writing the SSO code and implementing the process. Here is a code sample you can base your code on: [ssogenerator.pseudo](https://gist.github.com/cryptolos/76c07359b73c3b7f9eea25a6e22db620){target=`_blank`}. The script must be applied to the programming language you are using, where the codes need to be generated. The Subject ID listed in the pseudocode is the {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}. 7. Add the SSO code (`data-sso`) to the iframe. ## Visibility Control Because authentication uses the {{variable.Object_Contact}}’s {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}, the value in the {{variable.Object_Contact}}’s {{variable.Field_Contact_VisibilitControl}} field can be determined. The {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} field is located on the {{variable.Object_Event}}, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}, {{variable.Object_Contact}} (for {{variable.Feature_ExperienceCloud}}s), {{variable.Object_Attendee}}, and {{variable.Object_Session}} objects. The field’s standard picklist values include Member, Non-Member, VIP, and Press. Customized options can also be added. Once a value is chosen, dynamic {{variable.Object_Event}}s/{{variable.Object_EventItem}}s (Tickets) will be shown to only those {{variable.Object_Contact}}s with the matching value. For example, if an {{variable.Object_EventItem}}'s {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_VisibilityCo}} = "Member", only {{variable.Object_Contact}}s with {{variable.Field_Contact_VisibilitControl}} = "Member" will see the {{variable.Object_EventItem}}. Referencing the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}, also auto-populates the Attendee Form with the standard {{variable.Object_Contact}} fields. To read more about Visibility Control, [click here](/v1/docs/visibility-control). ## Iframes in the Community You can alternatively use iframes to embed an {{variable.Object_Event}}'s webpage onto your Community instead of using the Community component. This allows you to add customizations that are not currently supported by the Community component. Even though the iframe is inside the Community, it does not pull in the currently logged-in user as the Events Listing component does, so you will need to set up SSO authentication. ## Frequently Asked Questions **Q: Do I need to generate an SSO code for each {{variable.Object_Contact}}?** A: Yes, you must generate a unique SSO code for each {{variable.Object_Contact}}. No additional custom code is needed when using {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} as the identity provider. When using a 3rd party identity provider, you must generate the SSO code using the Context Key Blackthorn provides and each user’s {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}. **Q: Do I need to generate an SSO code for each Attendee?** A: No, {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s can’t use SSO authentication. {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s need to use the {{variable.Field_Attendee_AttendeeLink}} URL from the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record. **Q: Can I use AWS Key Management Service?** A: No. Different encryption libraries have different preferences for encrypting data. AWS Key Management Service is not compatible with Blackthorn’s solution. **Q: How do we enable authentication for a website?** A: If you are not using a {{variable.Product_Salesforce}}-associated method for logging into your website (e.g., Salesforce Authenticator), you must set up a process to pull the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}} from {{variable.Product_Salesforce}} into your website. **Q: Should the orgID and expiry value be encrypted in addition to the Contact ID?** A: Only the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}} must be encrypted. The org ID can be encrypted, but this will make the size of the key significantly longer. **Q: Should the encrypted value be stored and reused, or is generating a new one after each page refresh the correct approach?** A: The SSO key can be reused, and its expiration is based on the TTL used when generating it. However, creating a new key on every page refresh is a good practice. **Q: How do I identify an empty orgid and expiry?** A: Full stops (periods) before and after are required to identify an empty orgId and expiry. For example, if the orgID is blank, you will see something like: .12345.170000000 **Q: How do I encrypt/decrypt the Contact ID?** A: Use the example code below to create code to encrypt/decrypt the {{variable.Field_Contact_ContactID}}, which will then be used in the `data-sso` attribute: ```HTML import * as crypto from 'crypto'; import { getContextKey } from '../utils/contextKeyGenerator'; import { encode64 } from '../utils/encodeBase64'; import { DecodedContext } from '../types/sso-context'; const encodeContext = (context: DecodedContext, secretKey: Buffer): string => { const iv = crypto.randomBytes(16); const plaintext = Buffer.from([ context.orgId, context.subjectId, context.expiresAt ].join('.'), 'utf8'); const cipher = crypto.createCipheriv('aes256', secretKey, iv); const encrypted = Buffer.concat([iv, cipher.update(plaintext), cipher.final() ]); return encrypted.toString('base64').replace(/\+/g, '-').replace(/\//g, '_').replace(/=+$/, ''); }; ``` **Q: How do I auto-resize the iframe and use SSO authentication?** A: If you want to use auto-resizing on your iframe along with SSO authentication, add a manual listener to the page and parse through the {{variable.Object_Event}}s coming from the Blackthorn frame. This means the iframe is authenticated with a simple script, and the custom listener catches the {{variable.Object_Event}}s to resize. Below is an example script: ```HTML BTEmbed body{ overflow: hidden; } window.addEventListener('message', message => { console.log(message); console.log(message.data.req.method); console.log(message.data.req.params); let params = message.data.req.params if(message.data.req.method == 'CONTENT_SIZE_CHANGED'){ let mount = document.getElementsByClassName('bt-eventsapp-container')[0]; mount.style.height = params.height + 'px'; mount.getElementsByTagName('iframe')[0].style.height = params.height + 'px'; parent.postMessage(params.height); } }); ```
